purpose: MFPI aquaculture records for the version after 3.12: the fourteen 3.9 records unchanged, plus six records read in the original source on 2026-10-01 for species that gain a nutrition row (Korean national-name links, a literature row) or whose only missing input was the aquaculture record (team-lead decision 2026-10-01). One primary record per species.
rule: feasible = grow-out of this species documented from seed or juvenile to harvest, or through a full culture season, in a named system, region and period. A record whose trials stopped before grow-out is kept with feasible = false. Production counts alone are not proof. Flounder (71 land-based tank farms, Wando and Jeju, 2023), blue crab (commercial ponds in China, not Korea) and small yellow croaker (second-generation cultured broodstock; commercial culture rests on one uncited sentence) were added in 3.5 with those limits in each record. 3.7: research rearing of a species from egg to sexual maturity in a named facility and period counts as feasible = true (team-lead decision 2026-10-01, same standing as the croaker broodstock and cuttlefish trial records); the record states that it is not food production. After 3.12: six records added for 살오징어 (false), 다시마, 우뭇가사리 (research rearing to adult size, 3.7 rule), 꼬시래기, 해삼 and 시카메굴. 3.22: 괭생이모자반 added (Pang et al. 2008), tank culture of the species through a full generation to the long-line stage; research rearing, so the record says it is not food production.

food_support.record_id: Report No. BSPM55350-2205-3 (제출문 dated 2010. 10). The quote is from the 요약문 (PDF p.vi region). Also cited: the section on larval rearing from Geoje eggs in a 12 m³ PP tank at 강원도립대학, followed to 33 days post-hatch; the conditioning section (4 m PP circular tanks (10 t), deep ocean water at 5-6 °C); and PDF p.x (offshore cage and economics).
food_support.method: Experimental land-based flow-through tank rearing of wild-caught Pacific cod juveniles from set nets. The fish were weaned on frozen krill, then moved to formulated/moist feeds, in 4 m PP circular tanks (10 t) and 2 m³ tanks supplied with deep ocean water held at 5-6 °C. Larvae were also reared in a 12 m³ PP tank to 33 days post-hatch from eggs stripped from wild broodstock landed at Geoje. The planned offshore submerged-cage grow-out was never stocked with cod.
food_support.region: Republic of Korea, East Sea coast: Goseong-gun, Gangwon-do (KORDI Deep Ocean Water Research Center), with juveniles from set nets off Ohori. Eggs came from Geoje (Gyeongsangnam-do), and larval rearing was done at the Gangwon Provincial College fish-culture facility.
food_support.limitations: Recorded as not feasible: the only Korean record is a 2007-2010 pilot that reared wild-caught juveniles in land tanks; no fish reached market size, the planned offshore-cage grow-out was never stocked, and the economic analysis found NPV < 0. This was a pilot/experimental study with capture-based seed. The January batch grew from about 57 g to 154 g in 130 days with 46% survival. The March batch lost biomass. No fish reached market size. The offshore cage (installed at 24 m depth) was trial-stocked with yellowtail (방어) in October 2009; that stock died off in January 2010 from a sudden temperature drop and the cage panels were damaged, so the cod stocking planned for May 2010 was cancelled. The economic analysis of offshore-cage cod culture found NPV < 0 and B/C < 1 in the scenarios. There is no evidence of commercial production.
food_support.quote: 자연산 대구를 인공적인 환경에서 안정적인 사육기술개발을 위해 연중 10℃이하로 유지가 가능한 해양심층수를 이용하여 자연의 주 먹이인 크릴새우를 대상으로 육상 수조에서 먹이붙임 실험을 실시하였고

It shows technical feasibility with a large mortality constraint. The page does not say where the seed came from, so the earlier 'hatchery-size' wording was removed.

food_support.record_id: Final report TRKO201800002340, project no. 1525005011, DOI 10.23000/TRKO201800002340. The quote is in the Korean 초록 (cited as '출처 : 보고서 요약서 3p'). The table list includes '로프수하식 양성 시설 전경', '참담치 로프수하식 양성 전경', '로프수하식 양성시 수심에 따른 성장과 생존율' and '로프수하식 양성시 사육기간에 따른 생존율 변화'. The previously cited table name '로프수하식 로프 간양성장에서 참담치의 월별 생존율' does not appear on the page.
food_support.method: Rope hanging (suspended) grow-out culture (로프수하식). It outperformed basket hanging culture (채롱수하식). Raft-type intermediate nursery (the page writes '멧목식', a typo for 뗏목식) cut the nursery period by about 50% compared with 채롱수하식. Hatchery seed production used freshwater spawning stimulation. Horizontal-net culture (수평망식) on west-coast tidal flats was judged unsuitable.
food_support.region: South coast of Korea (남해안) for rope hanging grow-out. Grow-out sites in the table list are Geomundo and Dolsan-do, Yeosu (여수 거문도 / 돌산도 양성해역). The unsuccessful horizontal-net trial was on the west coast (Gunsan).
food_support.limitations: This is an R&D pilot and demonstration project, not proof of commercial-scale farming. The report says industrialisation would be effective 'if suitable sea areas are selected'. Only the ScienceON record page (Korean and English summaries plus table list) was verified. The full-text PDF was not opened.

food_support.method: Paralarvae reared in upwelling cages and 500 L tanks settled as benthic juveniles at about 20 days after hatching; separate feeding and shelter trials used adult octopuses of unstated origin
food_support.region: Tokai University, Japan
food_support.limitations: Rearing stopped at settlement; no grow-out of reared animals to market size or to maturity is reported in the abstract, so feasible = false under the 3.3/3.7 rule. Abstract level only.
food_support.quote: octopus paralarvae were observed to settle on the bottom of the upwelling cage at around 20 days of age after hatching

food_support.method: Mature squid spawned egg masses in a 300 m3, 6 m deep laboratory mesocosm (stratified 17-22 °C and uniform 22 °C trials); hatchlings were not reared beyond the paralarval stage
food_support.region: Hokkaido University, Hakodate, Japan (laboratory mesocosm)
food_support.limitations: Rearing stopped at the paralarval stage: paralarvae survived at most 10 days, so feasible = false under the 3.3/3.7 rule, as for 참문어. A 2026 study of wild paralarvae (Adachi et al., PLOS One 21:e0340579, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0340579) still investigates what they eat, and no full-cycle culture of this species was found. Adult squid held for 36 h in deep-ocean-water tanks (Hatano et al. 2023, Sci Rep 13:7591) is short-term holding, not culture. Abstract level.
food_support.quote: Paralarvae hatched at stage 30/31 and survived for up to 10 days

food_support.method: Research rearing: tetraspores germinated at 18-25 °C in a controlled indoor culture; juveniles at 18 °C were grown to adult size (over 10 cm) in more than a year, and subcultured thalli were kept for three years
food_support.region: Northern Taiwan (laboratory culture of local G. elegans)
food_support.year: published September 2024 (culture over more than one year; longevity trial three years)
food_support.limitations: Research rearing from spore to adult size in a named facility and period, counted as feasible = true under the 3.7 team-lead rule (as for 멸치). This is not food production: the authors plan outdoor culture next, and the abstract does not state reproductive maturity. A Korean provincial pilot (Jangheung, February 2006 to November 2007) reported in local news named the alga Gelidium amansii and gave no data, so it is not used.
food_support.quote: the juveniles cultivated at 18 °C reached adult size (more than 10 cm in length) after more than a year of cultivation

food_support.method: Outdoor 1200 L tanks fed with fishpond effluent in an integrated multi-trophic aquaculture (IMTA) system, stocking 3, 5 and 7 kg per m2 under two water flows; biomass harvested through the year

food_support.limitations: A European introduced population in a land-based IMTA farm, not Korean culture; the record shows that the species is grown through a full season in a named system. Biomass productivity peaked at about 372 g DW per m2 per week in May. Abstract level.
food_support.quote: The algae were grown in outdoor tanks in seawater with the addition of fishpond effluents

food_support.limitations: An overview by a fisheries research institute (Yellow Sea Fisheries Research Institute), not a single farm trial. It states that A. japonicus is the only sea cucumber cultured in China.
food_support.quote: If the individual weight of seeds is 10 g at the start of the stocking season, mean weight of 150 g will be reached in October to November of the same year.

food_support.region: Beihai, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
food_support.limitations: An experimental grow-out of hatchery progeny; the abstract does not name the culture structure. Commercial culture is reported elsewhere: Liu et al. 2021 (Front Physiol 12:713736) sampled cultured 20-month Kumamoto oysters of commercial size in Xiangshan Bay, Zhejiang, where the species is the main cultured oyster. Abstract level.
food_support.quote: compared the survival and growth of the hybrids to that of the two parental progenies during the grow-out period from July 2014 to July 2015

food_support.method: Indoor tank culture of the species through a full generation. Adult male and female plants were sampled in April 2007 at Xiaohuyu, Nanji Islands (27 27 N, 121 04 E), flown to the laboratory in Qingdao within 24 h and precultured in 80 L flow-through polypropylene tanks in tumble culture under reduced solar irradiance. Zygotes were collected on 6 June from one female plant and seeded onto a 0.5 m2 seedling collector; the seedlings were grown to 5-7 cm, re-inserted into a 2 cm nylon/cotton rope and grown on in a 1,000 L flow-through indoor raceway tank (lanes 400 x 40 x 40 cm, sand-filtered and ozone-treated water, 50% renewed daily, KNO3 10 and KH2PO4 1 mg/L every two days, long-lines hung at the surface at 15 cm intervals). The paper reports that the seedlings reached the long-line cultivation stage and that the life cycle in culture was completed in 4.5 months.
food_support.region: Laboratory in Qingdao, Shandong, China; parent plants from Nanji Islands, Zhejiang, China
food_support.year: October 2007 to April 2008 (raceway run); parent plants sampled April 2007, zygotes seeded 6 June
food_support.limitations: Research rearing for seedling production, not food production: the paper reports no harvest, yield or cost, and the grow-out stops at the long-line cultivation stage. It is counted feasible = true under the 3.7 rule that research rearing of a species through its life cycle in a named facility and period counts, the same standing as the 우뭇가사리 and 다시마 records. The work is Chinese, not Korean, and the parent plants are a Zhejiang population.
